Definition: from G1909 and G916; to be heavy upon, i.e. (pecuniarily) to be expensive to; figuratively, to be severe towards:--be chargeable to, overcharge.
BiblicalUsage: Epibareo means to be heavy upon, to be chargeable, to burden. Paul says he would not overcharge the Corinthians with grief over one man's sin, and that he worked night and day so as not to be chargeable to the Thessalonians.
TheologicalSignificance: The gospel is free, and the messenger should not make it costly. I hold that Paul's care not to burden the church is a model for every minister, and I should watch my own weight on the people I serve.
